prompt: Implement mean squared error, the classic loss function comparing predictions to actual values. Complete the mse method in the starter file.
explanation: Mean squared error measures how far predictions are from reality: square each difference (so under- and over-shooting both count positively), then average. Squaring also punishes large errors more than small ones, which is why MSE is the default regression loss in machine learning. Store the difference in a local variable and multiply it by itself -- no Math.pow needed.
hints: Loop over the indexes; compute double diff = predicted[i] - actual[i]; each time.
Add diff * diff to a running sum -- squaring makes negatives positive.
After the loop, return sum / predicted.length (the mean).
